# Checkpoint D: reviewed final test results

**Status:** Post-evaluation review of the original Gate C frozen test run. This is the authoritative final report. [final_test_results.md](final_test_results.md) is the preserved report generated by that first run; [final_test_metrics.json](final_test_metrics.json) is its machine-readable record. The charts below use that saved JSON. The test period was already inspected before this review; the fixed-setting reproduction described below checks the saved result and is not a new untouched evaluation or another selection cycle.

## Provenance and evaluation sequence

The owner accepted `count3_confidence_maximum` at Gate C. Before scoring test invoices, the run recorded source, prepared database, validation-output, policy, SQL and Python hashes, the holdout seed `basket-completion-v1`, bootstrap seed `20261031`, and the exact configuration in [frozen_config.json](../docs/frozen_config.json). The test metrics record that manifest's SHA-256, `f25fba1ae7cdb3db8bbff70fdb89a48cfd1c33c5353df904eed36dcdb80e83f4`. The original run then produced the saved test metrics and generated report. The prior session's tool record shows this order; current hashes still match every frozen file. No model, cleaning, split, candidate, or prepared-data change is recorded after test inspection. This review adds charts and documentation only. Most repository files are uncommitted, so Git alone cannot independently prove the sequence or provide an immutable timestamp.

The validation search used exactly the approved eight settings: minimum pair count `{3, 10}` × score `{confidence, lift}` × aggregation `{maximum, sum}`. The selected setting was based on validation (717/3,432 combined hits versus 77/3,432 for popularity). These are **selection-period findings**, not final test evidence. A validation rerun after an evidence-order determinism fix produced byte-identical metrics; no ninth setting was tried. The sensitivity used only the selected setting.

The frozen test evaluator reads the primary SQLite database in read-only mode. It obtains the popularity catalog and ranks from eligible training baskets; SQL pair counts and directional confidence `count(candidate, visible)/count(visible)` also use eligible training baskets only. Names are voted by training invoices only. Each test invoice yields one SHA-256 selected hidden product and the same visible basket for both methods. Both draw from the training catalog minus visible products. An unseen hidden target remains in the main denominator as a miss.

## Primary held-out result

The eligible test period contains **3,205 complete invoices**, each with 2–99 distinct products. Hit rate@5 counts invoices whose single hidden product appears among up to five suggestions.

| Method | Hits / invoices | Hit rate@5 | Difference from popularity |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Training-basket popularity | 64 / 3,205 | 2.00% | — |
| Association only | 589 / 3,205 | 18.38% | +16.38 percentage points |
| Association with labeled popularity fill | 589 / 3,205 | 18.38% | +16.38 percentage points |

The paired difference for the combined list is **+16.38 percentage points**. The prespecified 95% percentile interval from 1,000 fixed-seed paired customer-cluster bootstrap resamples is **+14.98 to +17.85 percentage points**. Known CustomerIDs are resampled as clusters; each invoice missing a CustomerID is a singleton. Training artifacts remain fixed. Missing IDs may conceal repeat customers, and this interval does not capture catalog or time-period uncertainty.

![Method comparison](figures/method_comparison.svg)

### Target groups and catalog reach

The primary training catalog contains **3,500 products**: head 350, middle 1,050, tail 2,100, ranked by training basket frequency and code ties. The groups below are assigned using those training ranks.

| Hidden target group | Test invoices | Popularity hits | Association-only hits | Combined hits | Combined hit rate@5 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Head | 1,132 | 64 | 274 | 274 | 24.20% |
| Middle | 1,083 | 0 | 238 | 238 | 21.98% |
| Tail | 637 | 0 | 77 | 77 | 12.09% |
| Unseen | 353 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.00% |

**Catalog target coverage** is the share of test hidden products present in the training catalog: **2,852/3,205 (89.0%)**. The **353 unseen targets** remain misses for all methods in the main result. On the separate known-target denominator of 2,852, popularity found **64 (2.24%)** and both association lists found **589 (20.65%)**.

![Training-defined popularity breakdown](figures/popularity_breakdown.svg)

### Evidence and fallback

**Association coverage** means at least one eligible association candidate before fill: **3,148/3,205 (98.2%)** invoices. **3,147** invoices had five association candidates and needed no fill. **One** had a mixed association/popularity list. **57** had no association candidates and used full popularity fallback. Thus **58/3,205 (1.8%)** used at least one popularity suggestion. Every final list contained five suggestions. The fill added **zero** hits, so association-only and filled hit rates coincide, although their suggestion lists differ on 58 baskets. Basket-level association coverage and suggestion-slot fill describe different things.

![Coverage and fallback behavior](figures/coverage_fallback.svg)

## Prespecified larger-basket sensitivity

The only policy change is the distinct-product ceiling, from `<100` to `<200`, across training and later eligible baskets. It adds **250 training baskets** (11,250 versus 11,000); its training catalog has **3,572** rather than 3,500 products, and its training pair table has **1,858,924** rather than 1,300,982 distinct pairs. Its popularity counts, display names and pair evidence are rebuilt from its own **training** baskets. Cleaning, product mapping, chronological boundaries, deterministic holdout, candidate restrictions, association score, tie breaks and labeled fill stay fixed. No setting was reselected.

| Test cohort | Baskets | Primary popularity | Primary combined | Sensitivity popularity | Sensitivity combined |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Common 2–99-product invoices | 3,205 | 64 / 3,205 (2.00%) | 589 / 3,205 (18.38%) | 64 / 3,205 (2.00%) | 553 / 3,205 (17.25%) |
| Additional 100–199-product invoices | 64 | — | — | 1 / 64 (1.56%) | 4 / 64 (6.25%) |

On the common cohort, the sensitivity combined difference from its popularity baseline is **+15.26 percentage points**; on the additional cohort it is **+4.69 percentage points**. Those 64 larger baskets are a different, small cohort, not a competing test configuration. The sensitivity excludes baskets with at least 200 products, so it does not settle the effect of the most extreme orders.

## Verification and interpretation

The saved percentages and differences recompute from integer hits and denominators. The frozen source, databases, validation outputs, policy, model code and test evaluator match their pretest manifest hashes. Independent reads of all test invoices reproduced the hidden-target groups, known/unseen counts and 64 popularity hits. The unchanged fixed evaluator was run again **after inspection** solely to check the saved primary metrics; no setting was searched or changed. All 13 hand-verifiable unit tests pass. The chart script asserts the count relationships before rendering and draws only from the saved metrics.

The first frozen test run is a held-out evaluation according to the available session record: model selection used validation, and the freeze preceded its first test scoring. The uncommitted repository does not independently establish the exact time order, which limits provenance certainty. This review and its reproduction are normal inspection of an already observed result, not post-test tuning.

The measured association method recovered more hidden products than popularity on later gift-retail invoices, with lower recovery for tail products and none possible for unseen targets. This is offline reconstruction of completed baskets. It does **not** show sales lift, product compatibility, next-click prediction, or superiority to a deployed recommendation system. The November–early-December test period differs seasonally from training; missing customer IDs may understate cluster dependence.
